He has your exact location and can guide you. He knows your dreams and your gifts. He knows when you feel alone and what your questions are. He knows your challenges and how to turn your weaknesses into strengths. He knows everything and knowing everything about you does not make him love you less. I suggested he choose just one home given our schedule limitations. Technically, he honored the request. After nearly two hours of listening, going right through our next meeting, I began to better understand their struggles, and I could feel their heartfelt strivings, and when I invited them to come to stake conference that evening, each one of them accepted, resisting the impulse to initially respond, built common ground, which allowed me later to teach from a place of love. clips.transcript: In the late 1980s, Mr. Martin developed severe heart failure. Despite the most advanced medications available, his heart couldn't adequately support his circulation. He would die without a heart transplant. He became my team's patient, and the weight for a donor heart began. His condition worsened, and mechanical pumps were implanted to sustain his life. A few days later, Mr. Martin's liver, kidneys, and lungs began to fail. If a donor heart didn't become available soon, he would surely die. One became available, and Mr. Martin received a transplant. Surprisingly, this new heart didn't work well, and his condition was now even worse. After a couple of days, the situation seemed hopeless, and we were preparing to withdraw our life support. While discussing the limited options with Mrs. Martin, I was notified that another donor heart was available. This donor heart was considered marginal and wouldn't be used for any other recipient in the country. With Mrs. Martin's consent, we decided to use this marginal heart for a second transplant. Fortunately, this marginal heart functioned beautifully. Within hours, Mr. Martin's liver kidneys and lungs began to recover, and the mechanical pumps were removed. Ten days later, I walked into Mr. Martin's hospital room knowing that he'd be discharged from the hospital the next day. He was sitting on his bed, gripping his breakfast tray, and was clearly irritated. I asked what was wrong. Through clenched teeth, Mr. Martin replied, "The oatmeal isn't hot, and the milk isn't cold." For the past three weeks, Mr. Martin had hovered near death, yet was now complaining about the hospital food. I think when you go through something like Mr. Martin did, you use up all your coping coupons. And I don't think anybody should be tortured with oatmeal, regardless of temperature. But at that moment Mr. Martin focused on the cold oatmeal in front of him, and seemingly dismissed the miracle he'd experienced. He lost sight of the bigger picture, both where he had been and the promise the future now held. Me too, can easily fall into the same trap.

clips.transcript: Now, you may ask, how can this be the case if a temple marriage does not endure? The revealed doctrine of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints does not address all details of and nuances about such cases. I do not know and cannot explain precisely how and when promised blessings are received, But I do know promised blessings will be received. clips.transcript: I began with a short story. Once a man wanted to visit family members in a distant country, he planned his trip packed his suitcase and traveled by airplane to the city where his relatives lived. The man excitedly exited the airplane and walked to the passport control checkpoint. He had a valid passport issued by an authorized agency of his country's government. He presented his passport to a border official who verified the man's identity, nationality, and reasons for visiting the country. But the man had not taken good care of his passport. The personal information page had been stained and damaged, and a ripped page had been repaired in an unauthorized manner with tape and glue. Consequently, the border official rejected his passport and refused to provide the stamp necessary for him to enter the country. The man was disappointed and perplexed about what he should do next. The lesson of this story is quite simple. The integrity of a passport must be maintained over time. Holding a valid passport provided the opportunity for the man to enter the country. But the passport alone did not guarantee he actually would be allowed to enter the country. Of course, this simple analogy has limitations.

clips.transcript: father teaches us about his love. While at a church meeting last year, I received an impression to do what the teacher was doing. So in the text, I asked my wife to find a baby picture of each of our children. When I got home, we sat down and showed my kids their pictures. I told them that there are no words to fully express the love we felt But when they were born, including the day each picture was taken, I then asked, "As of the date of this picture, what had you done to earn our love?" They lowered their eyes and said, "Nothing." I asked them to look up and said, "You are right. You did nothing to earn our love. By that same token, there is nothing you can ever do that will unearn or remove that love from you. You did not earn it, you cannot lose it, it is yours forever. I continued, we need you to always remember that what we feel is but a small fraction of what our Heavenly Father feels for you. You are His child and He loves you. He loved you before you were born. He loves you today and He will love you tomorrow. He wants you to prepare to be like Him. You must never forget this. We hope this understanding gives you courage to do your best to trust Him and to live up to your potential. We also hope it gives you the strength and the humility to come home when you need to. Because no matter what has happened, you can always come home just as you can always turn to your Father in heaven. There were tears in tender hearts as the Holy Spirit bore witness that this was true. I referenced my children, but for you it might be a special love.

She asked to complete her 11th grade through a homeschool program. My wife found an excellent school, asked me if I would stop by the Registrar's Office and submit her remaining enrollment documents. When arriving, I handed the paperwork to the registrar. She passed a document back to me, pointed to a line at the bottom and asked me to write my daughter's name and sign above it. However, my mind was preoccupied. I mistakenly thought she had instructed me to write my name. With full confidence I wrote, James Fontone and signed. A few seconds later, I realized my error. Well, I thought, no big deal, this is an easy fix. You see, our youngest daughter's name is Amanda James Fantoni. So I simply added Amanda right before my own name, and the error was quickly fixed. Later, in a quiet moment of reflection, A profuse.

clips.transcript: So our family experienced a sudden trial in the Lord's deliverance as we drove in two cars to begin our service as mission leaders. While driving in a construction zone, two large tires came loose from a semi-truck and struck both cars at high speed. The airbags deployed, the cars were destroyed, and we were left stranded on the roadside wondering why this had happened when we had left everything to serve the Lord. In that moment, the Spirit brought us peace. Everything would be all right. We were not immediately delivered from the trial, but that assurance gave us hope in the deliverance that would come. With the help of many wonderful people, we arrived on time and began our mission without serious injury. The experience on that freeway illustrates a scriptural pattern of divine deliverance.

clips.transcript: Sincere seeking means turning toward Heavenly Father in Jesus Christ through heartfelt prayer, purposeful fasting, and scripture study. Alma's people, in bondage, began to cry mightily to God. King Darius fasted through the night as he waited for Daniel's deliverance from the lion's den. clips.transcript: "than I ever thought possible." That realization came in 1998, when in a very weak moment, my running partner, Ted, somehow talked me into entering a 100-mile ultra-marathon race. Now clearly, I was not only out of my league, but possibly out of my mind for saying yes. Sure, I'd run a few marathons before, but not four of them back-to-back. Well, everything about it seemed impossible, except for one thing. And that was that Ted believed I could do it. And that mattered to me because he'd completed the race himself many times, so he knew every twist of the trail. And he also promised that if I would put in the training that he would be there to run with me through the second half of the race, when fatigue, blisters, and especially self-doubt would become my worst enemies. All race day arrived, and setting off in the pre-dawn hours, I quickly realized that this was much bigger than me, but somehow I kept moving, even through the withering heat of the afternoon, one slogging suffering step at a time. And then, with more than half of the race still ahead of me, and with daylight and my hopes fading, sure enough, Ted showed up. Now with Ted's patience, persistence, and my unceasing silent prayers, we miraculously ran, actually make that trudged to mile 90. Morning had just barely dawned. There were just ten miles remaining. But I was completely sapped, running on empty, as it were. Collapsing in the shade of a tree, I looked over at Ted, and quietly, but certainly said to him, "I give up." Even as my words and that resignation settled into the morning air, I guess I got what you could arguably call the world's first ever TED talk. And in a gentle reassuring tone, he reminded me of the months of preparation and those early morning runs. He then kneeled down, looked me in the eye, and said something I will never forget. "I know you can do this, Mike, "and I'm going to get you there." Well, those simple, sincere words sparked something inside me. And after a few more minutes, I did. I got to my feast, and at first I walked, and then I hobbled into, well, a pretty solid shuffle. And somehow, step by step, together, we conquered those last 10 miles. The impossible now looked possible. but about a hundred yards from the finish line. Ted suddenly reached out and grabbed my hand. Congrats, man, he said, you did it. And with that, it began to peel off even as I begged him to finish beside me. But he simply smiled and added, this is your race to finish, which I somehow did. Well, a week or so later, a photograph from the race arrived in the mail. miraculously, a friend captured that exact moment when Ted and I parted ways. But it also revealed a startling secret. You see, as I look closer, I saw what Ted really did for me that day. Much to my astonishment, I saw that he wasn't only carrying his water. He was carrying two of my water bottles and my pack, which he dutifully toted every step of those last 10 grueling miles. Somehow there on the side of the trail with me in deep despair and ready to quit, he quietly lightened my load, strapping my hydration pack to his own waist. And without fanfare or fuss, he simply shouldered my heaviest burden. Well, marveling at his benevolence, my thing.

By his grace, we can trust and expect in his constant care. And because God knows our prayers even before we ask him.

clips.transcript: Sometimes, we expect the Lord's places to come the way we would wish, rather than in his own way and timing. After a sacrament meeting, a faithful sister shared that her testimony of the love-tiding had begun to weaken. She explained that although she had always paid a full tie, she had never received the job promotion she had hoped for. or even the salary increase she deserved. The council I gave her is the same council that I share with you today. In his address, the windows of heaven elder David A. Bernard tapped. As we leave the love tiding, we often receive significant but subtle places that are not always what we expect, and easily can be overlooked. Elder Bernard's words prompted me to make a list of the blessings I have received through faithfully paying my tidings. The Holy Ghost helped me recognize many blessings. I have enjoyed studying employment for many years. My wife, my children, and I have been blessed with good health. Our home and temporal possessions have been preserved even during difficult times. The Lord has blessed me with the ability to manage my time and resources so I could obtain an education. I have developed the gift of gratitude by learning to appreciate the Lord's hand in each of his tender mercies. I have learned to recognize the influence of the Holy Ghost when making important decisions in my life. these blessings, both temporal and spiritual, and many others are evidence that the Lord has indeed opened the windows of heaven and pulled out His promised blessings in abundance. I invited that sister to write her own list of the significant yet subtle places the Lord had given her blessings that are often easy to overlook. Later, I heard another faithful sister share in a sacrament.

clips.transcript: A few weeks ago, President Ochtdorf took me aside and said, "Patrick, your talks, they're okay, but where's the aviation?" So here's just a little aviation. I spent much of my childhood at boarding school in England, looking up at aeroplanes crossing the sky dreaming of flying home to my parents thousands of miles away in Arabia, I yearned to fly. I wanted to become a fighter pilot. The Royal Air Force was recruiting pilots and the fastest way for me to fly was to learn to glide. A glider is a lightweight aircraft with long slender wings and no engine that stays aloft by riding within, rising currents of air. So in my mid-teens, I spent part of two summers at Nairfield in Oxfordshire, learning to fly a glider with the air force. First, I learned to fly straight and level, then make stable turns, to take off, towed by a tugplane and finally to land safely back at the airfield. Only then was I ready to learn to stay in the air, climb and eventually soar all without an engine. The crucial skill in gliding is finding rising air. You cannot see it, but you can see what it does. I was taught to look for cumulus clouds because they often mark where warm air is rising and I learned to fly toward them. But even more important than using visual cues to find rising air is to learn to feel it. While flying along, I would begin to feel that I was being lifted by an unseen force. The rising air is called lift. One wing would tip upward and I would turn toward it into the lift. I was taught how to stay in lift, circling upward, gaining altitude, and often join other pilots who had found lift, climbing within the same invisible rising column of air. To be flying is fantastic, but climbing in lift and soaring with no engine is almost beyond description. For me, it was beautiful. with only the whistle of the wind, the occasional creak from the glider, and the magnificent sensation of being drawn upward. Just as there is rising air, there is also sinking air, helpfully called sink. It likewise cannot be seen, but it can be felt, and I quickly learn to avoid it. Gliding into sink can feel like falling sometimes quickly. it shortens the distance you can fly and may threaten the safe landing. When I encountered sync, I learned to take to turn away decisively. A decade after those gliding days and not far into my journey of faith, I recognized that principles of gliding I had learned in my teens have significant similarities with spiritual principles. We must avoid sync and find lift. At the heart.

clips.transcript: That's what the Savior did, it's what His prophet does, and it's what we do, isn't it? A few years ago, my wife and I were waiting to board a fight for a much-needed vacation. We arrived at the airport early, and I put my earbuds in and started reading a book thankful for a few quiet moments to myself. Before long, I glanced up and saw a young missionary sitting across from me. He looked frightened and anxious. His eyes were closed, he was rocking back and forth, and tears were streaming down his cheeks. Clutched in his hands were his boarding pass and a digital alarm clock. After briefly imagining the various reasons a missionary might look so anxious, I returned to my book. But the spirit prompted me to look again. When I did, I saw his tear-filled eyes looking at me, pleading for help. Were you okay? I asked. In broken, timid English, explained that he was on the way to his mission. It was going to be his first time on an airplane alone and he was terrified. I learned he was a long way from his home country and he was holding the alarm clock to make sure he didn't miss the plane. Embarrassed by how slow I had been to help this elder, I explained that my wife and I would be on the same flight and we would make sure he made it on the plane. and I walked him to the gate and showed him the door he would go through and soon it was our turn to board. So Lindsay and I left him at the gate and took our seats. As the plane filled up, we anxiously watched for our missionary friend. There was no sign of him. I worried we had made a big mistake by boarding without him. Finally, there he was, like every missionary, last one to board. Still clutching his boarding pass an alarm clock making his way toward the only empty seat at the back of the plane. It was the seat next to me. We smiled at each other amazed at how God had arranged even a small detail like that one. Then the elder finally relaxing a bit fell fast asleep. When we landed I woke him and the panic returned to his face, as he worried about what to do next. Where was he supposed to go? What if there was no one waiting for him? Lindsay and I helped him get off the plane, walked him arm in arm not to lose him again, all the way to the baggage claim area. Waiting for him there were his mission leaders. Knowing what a special moment this always is, we were excited to see this new missionary being greeted by his leaders for the very first time. But to our surprise, our friend didn't run his mission leaders. Instead, he dropped his bags and gave Lindsey and me a big hug of luck, love and appreciation. What we did for that elder didn't require much of us, but this ordinary encounter became a divine appointment. We will always treasure. All we had to do was see the person God had placed in our path. Look with compassion rather than judgment and act. Brothers and sisters, let us pray every day for eyes to see the divine appointments God places before us. Let us put compassion into action and minister to the person in front of us. It's what Jesus did and it's what we do. In the sacred name we take upon ourselves by covenant, even Jesus Christ. Amen.
